claim: Exposure to drugs of abuse such as cocaine produces intense and long-lasting memories that are critical in the transition from recreational drug-taking to compulsive and uncontrolled drug use.
source: Exposure to drugs of abuse such as cocaine produces intense and long-lasting memories that are critical in the transition from recreational drug-taking to compulsive and uncontrolled drug use (Everitt, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Everitt, 2014.

claim: The experience of drugs of abuse depends on learned associations between drug-paired cues and the rewarding effects of these drugs.

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Sanchis-Segura and Spanagel, 2006.

claim: Preventing relapse following drug abstinence is impeded by the ability of drug-associated cues to persistently elicit drug-seeking behaviours.
source: Thus, preventing relapse following drug abstinence is impeded by the ability of drug-associated cues to persistently elicit drug-seeking behaviours (Belin et al., 2013).

claim: Conditioned drug cues may induce drug seeking and relapse behaviour.

claim: Cellular mechanisms and signalling pathways involved in normal learning and memory processes are usurped by addictive drugs in the brain.
source: In the brain, cellular mechanisms and signalling pathways involved in normal learning and memory processes are usurped by addictive drugs; hence, memories encoding drug-paired cues resist extinction and contribute to high rates of relapse (Nestler, 2004; Miller and Marshall, 2005; Torregrossa et al., 2011; Itzhak et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Memories encoding drug-paired cues resist extinction and contribute to high rates of relapse.

claim: Ras-ERK signalling has been implicated in both the acute and long-term effects of cocaine using different experimental paradigms that mimic drug addiction in humans.

claim: SL327 is the only available blood-brain barrier penetrating MEK inhibitor until recently.

evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Atkins et al., 1998 and Scherle et al., 2000.
